XXZ THERMAL TRANSFER: INDEPENDENT AUDIT
7 October 2026. Root-assigned audit; coordinates with tensor_contraction_audit.

DECISION AND STRONGEST RESULT

The proposed transfer survives the orientation, norm-error, nonhomogeneous-field,
and rational-bit audits. More strongly, the one-qubit field gates admit a direct
homogeneous LC lift. Thus the result needs Chen--Liu's homogeneous Theorem 5.1
and its rational-bit implementation, already independently reconstructed in
work/cycle2/counting_gate_audit.txt; it does not need the generic homogeneous-layer
closure in their Theorem 1.6. This is a conditional mathematical corollary with a
complete explicit reduction, not an implemented counting algorithm, external
proof certification, or certified-priority claim.

Let G be ANY loopless graph, including nonbipartite graphs, on n qubits, and let

 H = sum_(e=uv) [alpha_e(X_u X_v+Y_u Y_v)+gamma_e Z_u Z_v]
       + sum_v [b_v X_v+c_v Z_v],
 alpha_e >= |gamma_e|, b_v >= 0, c_v arbitrary,

with rational data. The physical Hamiltonian is -H. Set
 C=3 sum_e alpha_e+sum_v(b_v+|c_v|).
Conditional on Chen--Liu, the following classical algorithms exist:
 (i) relative partition-function approximation for Tr exp(beta H) in bit time
     polynomial in input length, numerical beta C, and inverse error;
 (ii) a standard bit-FPRAS for lambda_max(H), with no numerical norm overhead;
 (iii) sampling the computational-basis measurement law of the Gibbs state in
     total variation epsilon in the same numerical-parameter polynomial time;
 (iv) reconstruction, to trace-norm epsilon, of its reduced density matrix on
     any specified k=O(log n) qubits, and additive approximation of supplied
     norm-bounded observables on those qubits.
The sampling claim is for classical measurement outcomes. No global quantum
Gibbs-state preparation circuit is obtained.

TENSOR CONTRACTION AUDIT — 7 October 2026
Status: algebraic reduction/proofs below internally derived; FPRAS consequence CONDITIONAL on Chen–Liu arXiv:2610.06724v1 Theorem 5.1 and Remark A.4. Theorem 1.6 is an alternative import; an explicit homogeneous field lift below avoids its layer-reduction lemma. No FPRAS implementation or external priority certification.

STRONGEST CONCRETE RESULT
The two-measure exact-once theorem yields a conditional FPRAS for the full thermal trace of easy-plane XXZ interactions with arbitrary Z fields and nonnegative X fields, on arbitrary graphs. It also gives a FULL relative-error FPRAS for their largest eigenvalue, polynomial in binary coefficient length without requiring bounded numerical coupling scale (Section 4c). The gate/trace reduction below is explicit, rational, and has multiplicative error without inverse partition-function dependence. This extends the named source C.17 EPR application, but novelty is not established. Separately, an exact six-variable cubic disproves even homogeneous multiaffine log-concavity closure under full complement; this blocks a blanket equality-tensor transfer.

1. EXACT HAMILTONIAN INTERFACE
Let G=(V,E) be any finite loopless multigraph, with n qubits. Given binary rational coefficients,

 H = sum_{e=uv} [alpha_e (X_u X_v + Y_u Y_v) + gamma_e Z_u Z_v]
                  + sum_v [b_v X_v + c_v Z_v],

assume alpha_e >= |gamma_e|, b_v >= 0, and c_v arbitrary. Given rational beta>0 and 0<epsilon<=1, estimate

 Z_H(beta) = Tr exp(beta H)

with relative error epsilon and success probability at least 3/4, or amplify to 1-delta. The physical Hamiltonian is -H if using the conventional exp(-beta Hamiltonian) convention. No bipartition, planarity, degree, treewidth, or spectral-gap assumption is imposed.

Define r_v=|b_v|+|c_v|,
 C=3 sum_e alpha_e + sum_v r_v,
 D=2C,
 A_e=3 alpha_e I + alpha_e(XX+YY)+gamma_e ZZ,
 A_v=r_v I+b_v X+c_v Z.

Every A_i is real symmetric, positive semidefinite, and entrywise nonnegative. Indeed the edge eigenvalues are 3alpha+gamma (twice), 5alpha-gamma, alpha-gamma, so 0<=A_e and ||A_e||<=6alpha. SOFT-INTERSECTION TRANSFER: XXZ FIELD/LAYER AND PRIOR-ART ADDENDUM
7 October 2026. Supplements soft_intersection_transfer.txt and independently
audits the XXZ target in tensor_contraction_audit.txt. Does not duplicate the
thermal product-formula proof assigned to that report and the thermal auditor.

STATUS
The local field inequality, homogeneous lift, exact contraction identity, and
product-unitary obstruction below are internally proved algebraic lemmas.
The resulting approximation algorithm is CONDITIONAL on Chen–Liu
arXiv:2610.06724v1 Theorem 5.1 and its rational-bit implementation in Remark
A.4. The imported FPRAS has not been implemented or independently certified
here. This is a consequential explicit corollary of that source, with no claim
of externally established novelty or a new independent counting theorem.

STRONGEST FINDING
Nonhomogeneous X-field gates do not require the general homogeneous-layer
closure in source Theorem 1.6. Their coefficients satisfy a stronger inequality
which permits a direct degree-two, multiaffine, log-concave lift. One uniform
matroid factor sums the auxiliary indices without changing the trace. Thus the
XXZ + X/Z-field theorem can import homogeneous Theorem 5.1 alone.

Exact quantum interface, using the source's maximum-energy sign convention:

 H = sum_{uv in E}[alpha_uv(XX+YY)+gamma_uv ZZ]
                      + sum_v[b_v X_v+c_v Z_v],
 alpha_uv >= |gamma_uv|, b_v >= 0, c_v arbitrary,
 Z_H(beta)=Tr exp(+beta H), beta>0.

E is an arbitrary loopless multigraph, with rational coefficients; the physical
energy Hamiltonian in exp(-beta K) is K=-H. No bipartition, width, degree,
gap, or high-temperature assumption is needed in this exact interface. A legal
vertex Z gauge extends it to signed XY couplings and signed X fields only when
the common sign constraints in tensor_contraction_audit.txt Section 4b pass.
Arbitrary incompatible transverse-field signs are outside the stated class.
